moat_against: Walmart (largest US grocer, own logistics) and Amazon same-day fresh expansion can compress share and take rate
DoorDash and Uber Eats encroaching on grocery from adjacent delivery networks
Low consumer switching costs — shoppers multi-home and retailers can insource or dual-source
Gross margin eroding: 75.3% (2024) to 73.7% (2025) to 72.6% TTM as ad publisher payments and cost of revenue rise
SBC is a large, rising real cost: $300M (2024) to $352M (2025) to $401M TTM, ~10% of revenue
moat_for: Leading third-party grocery marketplace — ~21.6% US online grocery share and >70% share of large baskets over $75
Retailer network effects across 1,500+ banners plus scale data from 1.6B lifetime orders
Enterprise platform (storefronts, fulfillment, Caper carts) embedded in retailer operations — real switching costs
Closed-loop advertising: ad revenue +16% in Q2 2026 to 2.9% of GTV, monetizing purchase intent a second time
ROIC proxy 22.3% (2024) and 21.3% (2025) with gross margin 75.3% / 73.7% — returns well above cost of capital in the clean post-IPO years
moat_justification: Leading third-party grocery marketplace (~21.6% US online grocery share, dominant in large baskets) with retailer network effects, an enterprise platform (350+ storefronts, Caper carts) that raises retailer switching costs, and a closed-loop advertising business growing faster than GTV. ROIC proxy was 22.3% in 2024 and 21.3% in 2025 with gross margin 73-75%, supporting a moderate moat — but the clean ROIC history is only two post-IPO years, gross margin has slipped to 72.6% TTM, and Walmart and Amazon can outspend and out-distribute it, so it is not a wide moat.
name: Maplebear Inc. dba Instacart
one_liner: High-quality, debt-free grocery platform, moat 6/10 — does not clear 15% at $49.83 on TTM owner's earnings (13.7% weighted IRR, IV@15% $43.86); it clears 15% at or below $43.86, with the bear case at 9.3%.
